payload.summary: Fix calc.multiply() so it returns the product a * b instead of the sum a + b. The existing test test_multiply (assert multiply(3, 4) == 12) currently fails and should pass after the one-line change.

tasks.title: Change multiply() to return a * b
tasks.description: In calc.py, the multiply(a, b) function currently returns a + b. Change the return expression to a * b so multiplying two numbers returns their product. Do not modify any other functions.

tasks.title: Run tests to confirm multiply passes
tasks.description: Run the test suite (e.g., pytest tests/test_calc.py) and confirm test_multiply passes along with the rest of the tests. Report any failures.

findings: calc.py line 12-13: def multiply(a, b): return a + b — the function returns the sum instead of the product. The bug causes test_multiply (tests/test_calc.py line 13-14) to fail because multiply(3, 4) returns 7 instead of 12. The fix is a one-line change in calc.py: return a * b instead of return a + b. No other functions should be modified.

changes: Changed multiply(a, b) return expression from a + b to a * b
test_commands: python3 -c "from calc import multiply; assert multiply(3,4)==12"

payload.summary: Ran `python3 -m pytest tests/test_calc.py -q`: 10 passed. Direct assertion `multiply(3,4)==12` also passed. Syntax check `python3 -m py_compile calc.py stats.py tests/test_calc.py` passed with no errors. The multiply() bug is fixed and all tests pass.

suggestions: Change is minimal and correct: multiply() now returns a * b, matching the requirement and the test test_multiply (3 * 4 == 12).
No other functions were modified; divide-by-zero guard and other arithmetic functions remain intact.
